solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Holiday-maker? Person getting half cut by river

indicators.note: by means next to, so the river's letters sit beside the halved word

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: only the first half of the word person is kept, the rest cut away

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker who has had a few drinks too many beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it trims PERSON to PER. The Cam is the river in Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone staying in a tent or caravan on holiday is an example of a holidaymaker; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: A togetherness comes with the departure of one relation

indicators.note: the departure of a letter means it leaves the word, so it is removed

parts.note: unity is a state of togetherness
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Togetherness lasts until one member of the group leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the departure of' takes I out of UNITY to leave UNTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a family relation, spelt here in its informal form.

clue.text: Set of instructions for scientific unit

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
the gram is a metric unit of mass

explanation.surface: A list of steps that a scientific department follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing term: a sequence of coded commands for a machine to carry out, in the American spelling.

clue.text: Possibly an extra sequence

definitions.meaning: in cricket, extras such as byes and wides are scored as ... not credited to a batsman
a series of things in succession, like a winning streak

explanation.surface: An additional series of events, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras (wides, byes, no-balls) add runs to the team total without the batsman hitting them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket score counted as an extra is one such scoring unit; a streak of cards or results is another sense.

clue.text: Work involving paintings maybe to some extent

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
paintings are one example of art

explanation.surface: A job that only partly involves painting pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like the start of the definition, but it is the wordplay; to ply a trade is to work at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in part, not wholly: a degree adverb.

clue.text: More inclined to moralise, having power and influence? That is right

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
reach is range or influence, as in the reach of the law
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone with power and influence asks whether they are being too sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of the adjective for sermonising: more given to lecturing others on morals.

clue.text: Old magistrate about to meet woman in garden

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
Eve was the woman in the Garden of Eden

explanation.surface: A magistrate of old goes off to meet a lady in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A reeve was a local official in Anglo-Saxon and medieval England.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval English chief officer of a town or district, who kept order: a historical official.

clue.text: Disappointment in the French community — about 500

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the community word goes round the number

parts.note: a town is a community of people
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A French town of about five hundred people proves disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts D inside TOWN, after its T, giving TDOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fails to meet hopes is a disappointment; the hyphenated noun is the common idiom for it.

clue.text: Statements as discharged nun meets canon

indicators.note: discharged suggests released and scattered, so the letters are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun who has been dismissed meets a cleric, and statements follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal public declarations are statements made to inform people.

clue.text: What sounds like terrible person working with colours

indicators.note: the clue says the answer is pronounced the same as a word meaning terrible

parts.note: dire means dreadful or terrible

explanation.surface: Someone who works with colours is apparently awful.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who colours cloth or yarn with dyes works with colours.

clue.text: Composer taking part after comeback — fellow yet to meet his match?

definitions.text: fellow yet to meet his match?

parts.note: J.S. Bach the German composer

indicators.note: comeback means the word is turned backwards, and after places it behind the composer

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A composer returning to a role, and a man still waiting for a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man has not yet found his match, that is, a spouse: a playful definition.

clue.text: Like one with skin problems needing surgeon in hospital unit

indicators.note: in places the surgeon inside the hospital unit word

parts.note: hospitals count capacity in beds
Joseph Lister, the pioneer of antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A patient with skin trouble needs a surgeon in the hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister was the Victorian surgeon who introduced antiseptics.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin covered with raised fluid-filled bubbles is a skin problem; the adjective describes someone suffering it.

clue.text: Trick by Greek character providing sea food

parts.note: a scam is a swindle or trick
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek pulls a trick by serving seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: Scampi in Britain are breaded langoustine tails, a pub-menu staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded Norway lobster tails are a popular dish of seafood.

clue.text: Catch a cold, turning up, then erupt furiously

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Catching a cold, then flaring up in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes CA from A + C; 'furiously' rearranges ERUPT into PTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize or take prisoner is to catch: a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Mean to have nurse at back of home

indicators.note: at the back of means the nursing word comes after the home word

parts.note: in means at home
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: A plan to have a nurse at the rear of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to mean to do something, as in I meant to call: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Action in football match to add as extra feature

definitions.meaning: the way play restarts when the ball goes over the touchline
to include something extra at no cost, as a bonus

explanation.surface: A football move that adds an extra flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: A football restart from the touchline is the noun sense; including a bonus gratis is the phrasal verb sense.

clue.text: Splash when soup initially meets dish

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of soup

parts.note: a platter is a large serving dish

explanation.surface: Soup slops over when it hits the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To spatter liquid noisily in drops is to splash: verb synonym.

clue.text: Feature of church to change, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the clue word is pronounced the same as the answer

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: Someone wants to change a feature of the church, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised table where communion is celebrated is a central fixture in a church.

clue.text: Some crushed in stampede

indicators.note: some means just part of the next word supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Some people were crushed in a stampede.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden headlong surge of people is a stampede: noun synonym.

clue.text: Some problems — we argue and use bad language

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A couple admit that during their problems they argue and curse.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse or utter profanities is to use bad language.

clue.text: Kitchen ingredient we'd cooked in novel pud — carrots

indicators.note: cooked in a novel way means reworked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A recipe for a strange pudding made with carrots.
explanation.walkthrough: The powder is a British storecupboard staple for making custard.
explanation.definitionFit: A packet mix of cornflour and flavouring used to make custard is a kitchen ingredient.

clue.text: Margaret turning up in strange petticoat

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters read upwards
in says the letters are concealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Margaret showing up in an odd petticoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds GEP across strange petticoat; 'turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional pet form of the name, as with Peggy for Margaret.

clue.text: Get angry as one of the top players, without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the player word goes round the hesitation

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis tournament
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A top player getting cross without any hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here has its old sense of outside; seeds are ranked players in tennis draws.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to become furious, from a bull's supposed reaction to a red cape.

clue.text: Good attempt to incorporate a new framework

indicators.note: incorporate means take in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A good attempt to include a new structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised steel structure supporting cranes or signals: an example of a framework.
